info.title: TimeWarp.Architecture Web.Server API v1
info.description:
## Routes outside this document

This document includes the web-server FastEndpoints operations, `GET /api/health`, and `GET` and `POST /api` (a rewrite alias of `/api/tip`, including `/api/`).

The discovery documents below are not operations. A missing path is this exclusion, not a missing route. Scalar ([/scalar/v1](/scalar/v1)) shows this note. Index: [/llms.txt](/llms.txt). The same list is `x-timewarp-excluded-routes`.

- `GET /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` — Static MCP server card. capabilities.tools is false. [/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json](/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json)
- `GET /.well-known/mcp.json` — Alias of /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json. [/.well-known/mcp.json](/.well-known/mcp.json)
- `GET /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` — Static Agent Skills index. [/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json](/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json)
- `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` — Unsigned A2A agent card. No JSON-RPC task endpoint. [/.well-known/agent-card.json](/.well-known/agent-card.json)
- `GET /.well-known/agent.json` — Alias of /.well-known/agent-card.json. [/.well-known/agent.json](/.well-known/agent.json)
- `GET /.well-known/webmcp.json` — Generated WebMCP document for the browser, not this REST API. [/.well-known/webmcp.json](/.well-known/webmcp.json) Free and discovery operations never return HTTP 402. HTTP 402 and HTTP 503 are documented only on GET and POST /api/tip and on GET /api/demo/metered-capability. This document, health, identity ceremonies, and other free routes are not payment challenges. The bare /api path is a discovery alias of the tip jar, not a separate operation, and follows the tip jar. Disabled or misconfigured payment returns 503 on those paid routes and does not return 402.

get.description: Requires bearer scope demo:invoke (JWTBearerAuth). Requires bearer scope demo:invoke. The scope authorizes the attempt. Payment is separate: 402 with PAYMENT-REQUIRED when unpaid, or 200 with a ledger debit when credit or settlement covers the call. Disabled or misconfigured payment returns 503 and does not return 402. Free and discovery routes never return 402.

200.description: Success Success debits the ledger. The body includes balanceAfter and fundingSource. Prepaid credit or a settled x402 payment produces 200 instead of 402.

The PAYMENT-REQUIRED header is an x402 v2 challenge: base64 JSON with x402Version, accepts (scheme, network, payTo, price), and resource.url. Challenge resource.url is /api/demo/metered-capability.

post.summary: Completes agent key registration by returning the signed challenge.
post.description: The client signs the UTF-8 prefix TimeWarp.Identity.AgentKey.Register.v1: followed by the raw challenge bytes from start-agent-key-registration, using ECDSA P-256 and SHA-256. It sends back base64url PublicKey (SPKI), Challenge, and Signature (RFC 3279 DER). The response returns PrincipalId and KeyId. Intentionally anonymous. This is the request that mints the agent's Principal on success — no human sponsor or prior session required by design.

default.description: Problem details. The status is the problem's own status, 400 when the handler sets none.

post.summary: Starts agent key registration and returns a challenge to sign.
post.description: Returns a base64url challenge. The client signs the UTF-8 prefix TimeWarp.Identity.AgentKey.Register.v1: followed by the raw challenge bytes with ECDSA P-256 and SHA-256, and sends back the base64url SPKI public key, the base64url challenge, and the base64url RFC 3279 DER signature on complete-agent-key-registration. Intentionally anonymous. Mints a one-time registration challenge; no prior identity to authorize against, and no human sponsor is required by design.

default.description: Problem details. The status is the problem's own status, 400 when the handler sets none.

post.summary: Completes agent token issuance by returning the signed challenge.
post.description: The client signs the UTF-8 prefix TimeWarp.Identity.AgentKey.Token.v1: followed by the raw challenge bytes from start-agent-token-issuance, using ECDSA P-256 and SHA-256. It sends back base64url KeyId, Challenge, and Signature (RFC 3279 DER) and the requested Scopes. The response returns AccessToken, TokenType Bearer, ExpiresInSeconds, Scopes, and PrincipalId. There is no refresh token. The agent may request only scopes an admin approved through the principal's roles or grants on the principal. identity:read is always allowed. An unapproved scope returns 403 naming those scopes and issues no token. Removing an approval does not revoke a token already issued (tokens last 15 minutes by default); the change applies at the next issuance. Intentionally anonymous. This is the proof-of-possession request that mints the bearer token — nothing to authorize against yet.

default.description: Problem details. The status is the problem's own status, 400 when the handler sets none.

post.summary: Starts agent token issuance and returns a challenge to sign.
post.description: Returns a base64url challenge. The client signs the UTF-8 prefix TimeWarp.Identity.AgentKey.Token.v1: followed by the raw challenge bytes with ECDSA P-256 and SHA-256, and sends back the base64url KeyId, Challenge, and RFC 3279 DER Signature on complete-agent-token-issuance. Intentionally anonymous. Mints a one-time token-issuance challenge; the agent has not yet proven possession of a key, so there is nothing to authorize against.

JWTBearerAuth.description: Opaque agent access token. Send it as Authorization: Bearer. Known scopes: credential:manage, demo:invoke, feedback:note, feedback:read, feedback:severity, feedback:status, identity:read. 401 and 403 bodies are application/problem+json. 401 WWW-Authenticate is Bearer when no credential was presented, or Bearer error="invalid_token" when a presented bearer was rejected. 403 WWW-Authenticate is Bearer error="insufficient_scope" only when the scope is missing, and is absent on a handler-level 403. To obtain a token, call these operations in order: start-agent-key-registration (POST /api/identity/agent/register/options), then complete-agent-key-registration (POST /api/identity/agent/register), then start-agent-token-issuance (POST /api/identity/agent/token/options), then complete-agent-token-issuance (POST /api/identity/agent/token). The token lasts 15 minutes. There is no refresh token. Reissue with the agent key before the token expires, or after a 401 invalid_token. The agent may request only scopes an admin approved (identity:read is always allowed); an unapproved scope returns 403 naming those scopes, and removing an approval applies at the next issuance rather than revoking a token already issued.
